issues.description: Runtime pin setuptools<82 in core/setup.py leaks a CI build workaround into the package's install_requires.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this as the central issue. setuptools is a build-time tool; pinning it in install_requires propagates a transient mmcv build constraint to every downstream consumer of the hyperopt extra. The cap belongs in CI scripts or build-system requires, not in the library's runtime contract.

issues.description: setuptools<82 pin duplicated across three files with no shared source of truth or consistent FIXME breadcrumb.
issues.detail: The same constraint appears in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. The shell sites reference mmcv#3325; setup.py does not. When upstream is fixed, the revert path is implicit and easily missed in one location. A shared constant or single annotated invariant would make the workaround auditable and reversible.

issues.description: Switch to pip --no-build-isolation for mmcv silently couples the build to ambient environment state.
issues.detail: Replacing mim with pip --no-build-isolation makes mmcv's build read whatever setuptools/wheel/torch is in the active env. It works only because setuptools<82 is pre-pinned, but the coupling is invisible. A one-line comment explaining why isolation is disabled would help the next maintainer remove the workaround.

issues.description: mmdet bump 3.2.0 to 3.3.0 and mmengine SHA-to-0.10.7 substitution are bundled silently under a setuptools fix.
issues.detail: The PR is framed as a mmengine/setuptools fix, but mmdet also moves a minor version and mmengine drops its prior torch-2.5 SHA pin without restating that 0.10.7 satisfies that invariant. These are separate risk surfaces; bundling them makes future bisection and rollback harder. Each deserves a one-line rationale in the commit body.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges: the CI-side changes are reasonably shaped, but a build-time setuptools<82 pin has leaked into core/setup.py's install_requires, propagating a transient mmcv workaround to every downstream user of the hyperopt extra. The same constraint is restated in three places without a shared source of truth or consistent FIXME breadcrumb, making the eventual revert fragile. Secondary concerns: --no-build-isolation implicitly couples mmcv's build to ambient env state, and the mmdet/mmengine version moves ride along with no rationale. No architectural rework needed — this is contract-hygiene cleanup on a CI hotfix.
